A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the variability in L2 gender acquisition and processing is not a result of a lack of knowledge of the grammatical system, but rather a result of the complexity of the L2 system itself, as well as the interaction between the L1 system and the L2 system.
L2 learners are not deficient in morphological processing, but rather that they are faced with the challenge of mapping a new system onto their native language.
gender variability in L2 production is not a result of morphological deficit, but rather of the interaction of lexical and syntactic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L2 learners’ inflectional accuracy in production is not necessarily reflected by their accuracy in comprehension, which is also affected by the speed of lexical gender assignment.
the L2 learner's gender processing is not a unitary phenomenon but a dynamic system of lexical and syntactic components.
L2 learners’ lexical and syntactic representations of inflectional morphology are not dissociated.
